subject: Commercial: Consumption protections, invoice cadence & surge surcharge clarification
messages:
From: Amelia Barnes <amelia.barnes@sablesys.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Tariq Ahmed <tariq.ahmed@sablesys.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 16:45:00 -0500
Subject: RFP clarify: invoice cadence and surge surcharge

David,

Thanks — quick clarifying questions on the commercial section. Two items that are blocking procurement:

1) Invoice cadence / true-up: For committed token programs, do you do monthly true-ups or quarterly true-ups? Sable prefers monthly reconciliation to align with our month-end close.
2) Surge surcharge: We saw language about a "surge surcharge" for usage above committed tiers. Can you outline how that surcharge is calculated (fixed multiplier vs. stepped bands) and whether it applies to short spikes (single-day) or to sustained overage within a billing period?

Can you also confirm whether surcharges are capped or whether there is an escrow/credit mechanism for one-off spikes during onboarding?

Attaching our RFP Q&A grid for reference. Appreciate a short summary we can include in the procurement appendix.

Best,
Amelia
Procurement Lead
Sable Systems

Attachment: sablesys_rfp_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Barnes <amelia.barnes@sablesys.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP clarify: invoice cadence and surge surcharge

Amelia — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up top, then a brief appendix.

Short answers:
- Invoice cadence: We support monthly true-ups by default for committed programs; customers can elect quarterly true-ups for administrative simplicity. Monthly true-up aligns with Sable's preference.
- Surge surcharge: We charge stepped overage bands on top of the committed unit price (not a single-day multiplier). For short single-day spikes that do not push you into the next billing band by month-end, we do not apply the higher band — we prorate against the month. For sustained overage within the billing period that moves you into a higher band, the higher rate applies to the incremental consumption in that band.
- Caps & protections: We offer a 30-day onboarding grace buffer (one-time, configurable) for initial spikes and an optional escrow credit facility (monthly drawdown up to X tokens equivalent) for enterprise customers on annual committed contracts.

Appendix (commercial mechanics):
1) Pricing model: base committed token rate (USD per 1k tokens) with tiered overage bands. Bands are defined on monthly consumed tokens. Each band has a pre-agreed multiplier relative to the commit rate (e.g., 1.0x for base, 1.25x for next band, 1.6x for >200% of commit). Discounts are anchored to the annual committed volume and model family (encoder vs. decoder; large-context models have a premium).
2) Single-day spike handling: single-day spikes are assessed at month-end. We compute monthly consumption; if the spike alone doesn't move you into the next band, you pay at the lower band for that spike.
3) Escrow / credit: For annual committed customers we can set up an escrow (pre-funded or capitalized via monthly draws) that can be used to absorb up to one month's worth of overage. Escrow terms are negotiated; unused escrow rolls to next period subject to amortization schedule.
4) Invoice cadence & true-up: default monthly invoices with line-item true-up for tokens used vs. committed. If customer elects quarterly, we aggregate months and perform a quarterly true-up with adjustment invoice.

I'll attach a compact commercial summary for inclusion in your appendix. Marissa / Karthik — tagging you both to confirm the band multipliers used in the example and whether the escrow wording needs legal review before we send formally.

Thanks,
David
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_commercial_summary_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: RFP clarify: invoice cadence and surge surcharge

David — thanks for drafting the response. A couple of legal/commercial notes before we send to the customer:

- Band multipliers: legal prefers putting example multipliers in the appendix with a clear "illustrative" label and a table linking bands to absolute USD per 1k tokens. Suggest we use 1.00x (base), 1.30x (band2), 1.60x (band3) in examples; final multipliers remain negotiable.
- Escrow: need confirmation from finance on whether we allow pre-funded escrow with monthly amortization vs. non-refundable escrow. Finance will want an explicit rollback mechanism for unused funds.
- One-time onboarding buffer: propose default 30 days free buffer for pilots < 90 days, but only once per account.

Karthik — can you confirm the market precedent on short spike handling? My view: pro-customer to not charge higher band for single-day spikes unless month-end totals bump them up.

If all good I'll send with the attached PDF and include the illustrative table.

-M

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Barnes <amelia.barnes@sablesys.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP clarify: invoice cadence and surge surcharge

Amelia — follow-up with clarified language and illustrative numbers attached. Quick summary of the changes per your ask:

- Monthly true-up is standard; we confirm monthly reconciliation for Sable.
- Surge handling: single-day spikes are prorated and will not be charged at a higher band unless month-end consumption crosses the band boundary.
- Illustrative multipliers included (1.00x / 1.30x / 1.60x). These are examples and will be negotiated in the commercial term sheet.
- Escrow: offered as an elective option on annual commitments. We propose a pre-funded escrow with monthly amortization; finance will propose final rollback language during contracting.

Next steps: If this wording looks good from procurement's side, can you confirm the preferred invoice cadence (we'll set to monthly by default) and whether you'd like us to put the illustrative table into the procurement appendix of the RFP? Once confirmed we can hand to legal for term-sheet language and DocuSign.

Best,
David
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_commercial_summary_v2.pdf (application/pdf)
